rationale: C21 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are personal commemorative letters organized around a long public career, increasing admiration, distinguished service in major responsibilities, and a closing hope that the nation will continue to benefit from the recipient's qualities. The overlap in phrasing and rhetorical sequence is substantially more concrete than generic congratulatory boilerplate. C18 is another close anniversary tribute centered on peace and long service, while C07 parallels the retrospective appraisal of historically significant public accomplishments, but neither matches the child's full structure as closely as C21.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In those years of enriching experience, you have gone on to ever increasing responsibility in the field of public service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I look anew, and with ever increasing admiration, upon your distinguished career. Few men in our country's history have been privileged to serve the nation in so many important capacities as have you
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the commemoration as a retrospective survey of an unusually long and progressively important career in national service, including the shared phrase “ever increasing.”

shared_material.child_excerpt: your accomplishments will establish you as one of the greatest of our Secretaries of State
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Few men in our country's history have been privileged to serve the nation in so many important capacities as have you, and certainly none has done so with greater brilliance and devotion.
shared_material.explanation: Each elevates the recipient through an explicit historical comparison emphasizing exceptional distinction and devotion.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also express my profound hope that the nation shall have the benefit of your experience and wisdom for many years to come.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: May you have many more years of happiness and health, and may we continue to have the benefit of your counsel and judgment.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close substantive and verbal match in the concluding wish: many more years during which the nation or administration may continue benefiting from the honoree's wisdom, counsel, or judgment.
